what: Cardinal Health distributes medicines to pharmacies and hospitals, and separately makes and sells its own medical products such as surgical kits, gloves and gowns.
customers: Pharmacy chains, hospitals, surgery centres and physician practices in the United States.
money: distributing branded, generic and speciality drugs
its own branded medical products and medical supply distribution
moat: One of three distributors handling almost all US drug volume, with a delivery network and generic sourcing scale that cannot be rebuilt.
risks: Margins are about one cent on each revenue dollar
Losing a large pharmacy contract moves results materially
The medical products business has struggled with cost inflation
Opioid settlement payments continue for years
opportunities: Return on invested capital near 29% because it uses little fixed capital
Speciality drug distribution and oncology services grow faster than the core
Cost programmes in medical products are improving that segment
watch: Segment operating profit, and whether the medical products business keeps recovering.
